topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, recaps practical sessions, and outlines the learning objectives and topics to be covered.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Cellular Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for testing oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Classifications and Mechanisms of Cancer Genes and Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated genes and illustrate how mutations alter cell cycle regulation and protein function through dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Forms and Mechanisms of Genetic Instability in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular pathways and cellular defects in DNA repair, replication, and chromosome segregation that produce sequence instability and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multistep Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited gene defects and the sequential accumulation of somatic mutations accelerate tumor development and influence cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with reading recommendations and a preview of the next lecture.
